description:
Rule: a runtime function that reads a binary is handed a proven binary. The proof is the extern's declared parameter type (binary/bitstring) plus .fz guards shaped like Elixir's function heads.

Changes:
- fz_binary_upcase, fz_binary_downcase, fz_grapheme_size and fz_binary_to_atom declare `binary` (today `any`).
- String.length gets an is_binary head.
- String.to_atom and String.to_float raise ArgumentError, for a non-binary and for bad content, before the extern.
- Delete the runtime's not-a-binary panics, aborts and sentinels (extern_binary.rs abort; about 25 paths).

Evidence: today String.length(1) and String.to_atom(1) SIGABRT on interp, JIT and AOT (Rust panic in extern "C"). String.to_float(1) raises FunctionClauseError in Float.fz_float_parse/1, where Elixir raises ArgumentError.

Acceptance: an oracle fixture runs each binary function on 1 and <<1::3>> inside rescue and matches Elixir on all three paths.

Page: https://claude.ai/artifact/7oEdkmwEoL8RVcfbYXPZzg (From: Binary Handling), approved by the user 2026-11-23 (relayed by Binary Handling). Owner: Binary Handling.
title: A binary function given a non-binary raises what Elixir raises
